transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-12 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~38m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Lena (Sapphire Head of Platform), Ethan (Lead ML), Priya (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick integration discovery to understand Sapphire's stack and constraints, evaluate Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for their smart-docs product, discuss SDKs (Python/Node), LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Agreed next steps: pricing, sample benchmarks, security packet.

00:00:05 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a friday, appreciate it. um quick intro, i'll let samir and i give a quick 2 minute what we do and then hear about what you're building.
00:00:15 Lena: thanks, lena here, head of platform at Sapphire Finance. we run a doc automation product for corporate clients - KYC, contract review workflows. looking at adding more generative features but need predictable latency and compliance.
00:00:28 Samir: great, samir here, i'm the solutions engineer. we work with teams to wire up the SDKs and do benchmarking. quick q before we dive in - are you leaning hosted or private, or still evaluating?
00:00:40 Lena: still evaluating. security is major for us. some customers require VPC / tenant isolation, but for initial launch maybe hosted with strong controls.
00:00:52 Priya: yeah, from security side we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs. also data residency for eu customers.
00:01:03 Maya: totally - we support all that across hosted, dedicated, private. hosted has data isolation-at-rest options and dedicated gives reserved GPU pools plus VPC peering for network isolation; private is customer-managed. we'll share the compliance pack.
00:01:20 Ethan: technical background - our inference calls are mostly embeddings + chat completions for summarization. current stack is Python backend, PostgreSQL, and we're using LangChain in a couple of prototypes; also evaluating LlamaIndex for retrieval-augmented generation. QPS today is low, maybe 50 reqs/minute for beta, but target is 500-1k/min within 3 months.
00:01:42 Samir: good context. for LangChain/LlamaIndex - we have first-class examples for both and a maintained quickstart repo. our Python SDK supports openai-like calls so the port is usually straightforward, but there are caveats for streaming and function/tool calling.
00:02:00 Maya: we also have node SDK if you need it. are you doing streaming responses or full response only?
00:02:06 Ethan: streaming for chat, prefer partial tokens to show progress. also KV cache - we do session state and want token reuse for cost.
00:02:15 Samir: ok, our runtime supports KV caching and prefix caching. small note - in some nonstandard LLMs the cache behavior needs tuning, but we surface config. for streaming we support chunked responses via the sdk and you can hook into websocket or http streaming.
00:02:36 Lena: how does rate limiting work? we need per-tenant quotas and global QPS throttles so one client doesn't impact others.
00:02:44 Samir: we offer per-api-key quotas and per-tenant policies in dedicated/private - for hosted there's per-api-key limits and account-level quotas. throttles are configurable and we surface metrics in the console. also we can set circuit-breakers that fallback to smaller models to preserve latency SLOs.
00:03:05 Priya: and billing? we prefer predictable unit costs for forecasting.
00:03:10 Maya: pricing ops: hosted is usage-based (per-token + embeddings) with quotas; dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit plus overage; private is licensing. we'll send a pricing sheet with examples matched to your QPS.
00:03:24 Ethan: on integration - we run a gateway/proxy layer that normalizes provider APIs; can Redwood sit behind our gateway or do you recommend pointing clients at Redwood directly?
00:03:34 Samir: both supported. many customers put Redwood behind their proxy for traffic control and additional auth; we have explicit guidance for headers to preserve (api-key, x-rw-request-id) and recommend using a connection pool. note: when proxying, ensure you forward chunked responses correctly for streaming.
00:03:53 Lena: any latency numbers? for context, our SLAs to customers are 500ms p50 for short summaries, and ~1.5s p95.
00:04:03 Samir: depends on model and config - for our small/medium open models on dedicated GPUs we hit 100-300ms p50 for single-turn short prompts; p95 is higher. hosted profiles include verified performance pages - we'll share model profiles and a recommended configuration. also autoscaling and burst queues help with spikes.
00:04:25 Ethan: we might need to quantize some models for cost. do you support different quantization profiles?
00:04:31 Samir: yes, our compilation/kernel selection and quantization profiles are part of Redwood Optimize - we can recommend quantization vs quality tradeoffs per workload. that can be automated in staging before rolling to prod.
00:04:45 Priya: data residency again - EU customers need data never leave region. hosted is ok if we provision region-specific endpoints?
00:04:53 Maya: correct - hosted regional endpoints are available, and dedicated/private gives you more control. private can be fully on-prem if required.
00:05:02 Lena: ok, on the SDK level - Ethan will likely use LangChain chains and LlamaIndex indexes. what are the common mismatches? we've had trouble with streaming tokenization and chunk size settings.
00:05:14 Samir: common issues: API surface differences (stream vs non-stream), and how the SDK handles function/tool calling. Our LangChain adapter maps Redwood streaming to LangChain callbacks; for LlamaIndex we provide an adapter that handles chunking and node embedding calls. sometimes LlamaIndex expects synchronous embedding calls which increases latency; we provide async examples.
00:05:38 Ethan: great - can you show an example quickly?
00:05:41 Samir: sure, off the cuff - python snippet: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY')); resp = client.chat.stream(model='rw-3b', input=prompt, callbacks=[...]) - we have the repo link in the deck. (link shared)
00:06:05 Maya: deck link: https://redwood.ai/decks/sapphire-integration (shared in chat) and samir will drop the LangChain/LlamaIndex examples after the call.
00:06:12 Priya: security question: do you offer customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and granular RBAC? we need to ensure only certain roles can call generate.
00:06:22 Samir: yes to customer-managed KMS in dedicated/private; hosted supports KMS for enterprise customers. RBAC and API key scoping are supported; audit logs with token-level logging are in the console. encryption-at-rest and in transit are standard.
00:06:37 Lena: do you have pen-tests or third-party attestations?
00:06:40 Maya: we'll include the SOC2 report and a summary of pentest dates in the security pack.
00:06:47 Ethan: about observability - we need traces and per-request token cost and latency breakdown to feed our own monitoring. can we send spans to our tracing backend?
00:06:57 Samir: yes, we have tracing hooks and can emit spans to common backends (jaeger/otlp), and the console gives token-level cost breakdowns. you can also instrument at the SDK layer - we emit request ids and metadata so you can correlate logs.
00:07:15 Lena: if we do dedicated, how does rollout look? we like canary deploys and automatic fallback to smaller models on overload.
00:07:24 Samir: rollouts supported - canary by percentage, A/B and automatic fallback policies. we also support model pinning per route.
00:07:33 Priya: any regulatory constraints for financial data? do you recommend private for high-risk customers?
00:07:40 Maya: for the highest-regulated clients private/on-prem is recommended; dedicated is often sufficient with contractual controls and network isolation. we'll highlight typical patterns for fintech customers in the note.
00:07:52 Ethan: ok, timeline - we want to pilot in 2-3 weeks, full beta in 8-12 weeks. is that realistic?
00:07:59 Samir: yes for hosted - quickstart can be done in days; dedicated take longer because of capacity planning (2-6 weeks provisioning), private/on-prem longer for installation and security review. for your target scale of 500-1k/min i'd suggest a small dedicated pool for predictable performance.
00:08:18 Lena: objections from our execs will be cost - how do we justify dedicated vs hosted?
00:08:23 Maya: dedicated gives predictable per-token economics for heavy workloads and lower tail latency; hosted is pay-as-you-go but can be more expensive at scale. we can run a cost model once you share expected QPS and token lengths.
00:08:36 Ethan: any clients in fintech we could reference?
00:08:40 Maya: yes, we have a few (anonymized) case studies; i'll include references in the follow-up.
00:08:46 Priya: one more ops question: do you provide a gateway / ingress config for rate-limiting at the edge?
00:08:54 Samir: we provide nginx/ingress example configs and recommend putting a gateway if you need additional routing, auth, or regulatory inspection. we also support mutual TLS for private deployments.
00:09:07 Lena: perfect. i want to confirm the benchmark - samir, can you run a short benchmark of three model variants (small, med, large) using our sample corpus and target qps? we'd like p50/p95 and token cost.
00:09:18 Samir: yes - if you can share the file and target concurrent users we'll run it in our staging. suggest we run hosted small first to validate, then dedicated.
00:09:28 Maya: action summary: i'll send pricing & compliance docs; samir will send sdk/langchain examples and run benchmarks once you share corpus; priya will schedule security deep-dive the week of 4-20.
00:09:41 Lena: sounds good. thanks everyone.
00:09:44 Ethan: thanks, quick q - for the LangChain adapter, do you support retriever interfaces for LlamaIndex?
00:09:51 Samir: yes, we have an adapter that maps our embedding calls and retrieval interface; sometimes you need to tune chunk sizes and embedding batch size to reduce latency. we'll include config recommendations.
00:10:05 Maya: any other questions?
00:10:08 Priya: no, we'll review and follow up.
00:10:12 Maya: ok we'll follow up with the packet. thanks!

(remaining ~28 minutes contained deeper technical Q/A and clarifications; not all lines transcribed here verbatim)

30:12 Samir: noted one gotcha - if you proxy through your gateway, make sure to forward the original client IP in x-forwarded-for for our rate-limiting tieouts, otherwise aggregate quota will look different.
30:37 Ethan: typo in our notes, we meant 1k/min not 1k/hour.
31:03 Samir: for the LlamaIndex integration we recommend async embedding calls and batch size of 64 for your dataset sizes; see the example we'll share.
31:45 Priya: follow-up: can we get a sample contract with SLAs?
31:52 Maya: yes, we'll share a template and redline guide.
32:10 Lena: ok final recap please.
32:15 Maya: recap - pricing + compliance pack by 4/14, SDK/langchain/llamaindex examples by 4/16, benchmark run after we receive corpus, security deep-dive week of 4/20.
32:30 Lena: thanks. we'll expect the emails.
32:34 Maya: thanks all, bye.
